LESSON: LETTER RECOGNITION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.1: Letter recognition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Letter recognition, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Where can we read letter sounds from? 2. Which letter sounds do you like most?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify correctly letters of the alphabet from print using their names,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Letter recognition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. distinguish between the lower case and upper case letters of the alphabet,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Letter recognition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. participate with pleasure in letter recognition activities. ● Listen to letters of the alphabet being read either from a digital device or by the teacher, ● Imitate reading letters of the alphabet in bits. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to imitate. ● Recognize letters of the alphabet in lower case, ● Recognize letters of the alphabet in upper case, ● Individually or in small purposive groups engages in letter recognition games, e g, letter fishing games, letter sorting, letter hunting games, ● Compete in letter recognition games and encouraged to show fairness in winning and acceptance in losing, ● Chant rhymes to match letter names with letter sounds (letter a, sound /a/, letter b, sound /b/. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech to chant. 1. Where can we read letter sounds from? 2. Which letter sounds do you like most? 70 ● Sing songs or recite poems related to letter recognition, while displaying letters. Learners with speech difficulties could hum, mime, tap, clap or move with the rhythm of the song.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Letter recognition in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

   Letter recognition helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech to chant. 1. Where can we read letter sounds from? 2. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Letter recognition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learn independently as the learner engages in letter recognition games.

Values:
● Responsibility is developed as the learner becomes more and more aware of letters and sounds and can read and recognize

these even while out of class.

● Unity is developed as the learner together with others chant letter sound and letter name rhymes to achieve a common goal

of recognition of the two.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Self-awareness is enhanced as the learner becomes more aware of own abilities in relation to reading and recognizing letter

names and letter sounds.

Link to other Learning Areas: Creative Activities as learners sing song or recite poems related to letter recognition.

Suggested learning resources: Digital device, charts, pens, colour pencils used to identify letter sounds
